scope: BPI control-plane rule application and independent runtime-readiness receipt transaction visibility, restart replay, event-time ordering, idempotency and DLQ acceptance

phases.name: committedRejectedAndListenerRestartReplay
phases.expected: REJECTED revision 2; exact replay after listener restart keeps application inbox 1 and audit 1

phases.name: committedAppliedAndStaleRejected
phases.expected: APPLIED revision 3; stale distinct REJECTED is recorded in inbox but cannot change APPLIED or add audit

phases.name: runtimeDegradedAndListenerRestartReplay
phases.expected: application remains APPLIED; runtime becomes DEGRADED revision 4 with point-catalog reason; exact replay after listener restart adds no row

phases.name: olderRuntimeReadyIgnored
phases.expected: older distinct READY is recorded in readiness inbox but runtime remains DEGRADED revision 4 and audit is unchanged

phases.name: newerRuntimeReadyAndExactReplay
phases.expected: application remains APPLIED; runtime becomes READY revision 5, clears degradation reason, records CATALOG-READY and exact replay is idempotent

phases.name: topicSpecificPoisonPayloadDeadLetter
phases.expected: application poison reaches application DLQ and runtime poison reaches runtime-readiness DLQ with original bytes and source-topic header; no business mutation

verificationSql: SELECT application_status, runtime_readiness_status, runtime_readiness_deployment_id, runtime_readiness_reason_code, runtime_point_catalog_event_id, runtime_point_catalog_source_revision, revision FROM bpi.bpi_outbox_events WHERE tenant_id = :tenant AND id = :publication_id;
SELECT source, count(*) FROM bpi.bpi_inbox_events WHERE tenant_id = :tenant GROUP BY source ORDER BY source;
SELECT action, before_revision, after_revision FROM bpi.bpi_audit_events WHERE tenant_id = :tenant AND object_id = :publication_id ORDER BY after_revision;
limitations: Embedded Kafka is real broker protocol execution but is not the target three-broker cluster.

A transactional Kafka producer emulates the Flink checkpoint sink; actual Flink 2.2.1 MiniCluster checkpoint behavior is proven separately by metadata/bpi-rule-application-flink-kafka-acceptance.json.
The test directly asserts PostgreSQL rows before its test-owned marker cleanup; no acceptance marker rows are intentionally retained afterward.
The acceptance does not cover a browser-to-Java-to-Kafka/Flink/PostgreSQL round trip or claim target-environment deployment or production readiness.
